title.value: Learning to Guide and to Be Guided in the Architect-Builder Problem
title.justification: The title is explicitly stated at the beginning of the paper and throughout the text as a central theme of the research.
title.quote: LEARNING TO GUIDE AND TO BE GUIDED IN THE ARCHITECT-BUILDER PROBLEM

analysis.description: This paper introduces the Architect-Builder Problem (ABP), where an architect guides a builder to solve tasks without direct rewards or predefined communication protocols. The architect knows the goal and can only communicate with the builder through messages, while the builder acts but has no knowledge of the task. The authors propose the Architect-Builder Iterated Guiding (ABIG) method as a solution, which leverages interaction frames and shared intent to allow agents to learn and generalize communication protocols across tasks.

type.justification: The paper presents experimental results, reinforcement learning scenarios, and comparisons demonstrating the empirical nature of the research.
type.quote: We analyze the key learning mechanisms of ABIG and test it in a 2-dimensional instantiation of the ABP where tasks involve grasping cubes, placing them at a given location, or building various shapes.

name.justification: The paper is centered around interactions and learning between multiple agents in a reinforcement learning context.
name.quote: sets this work apart from Reinforcement Learning (RL) and even Multi-Agent RL (MARL) where explicit rewards are available to all agents.

name.justification: The task involves developing communication protocols between the architect and builder, a core aspect of emergent communication research.
name.quote: Such learning should only rely on high-level communication priors and be able to handle a large variety of tasks and meanings while deriving communication protocols that can be reused across tasks.

name.justification: The problem setting is discussed in relation to HRI challenges such as Brain Computer Interfaces (BCI), focusing on human-agent interaction without predefined communication.
name.quote: These constraints make ABP an appealing setting to investigate Human-Robot Interaction (HRI) (Goodrich & Schultz, 2008) problems where “a learner tries to figure out what a teacher wants them to do”.

name.justification: ABIG is explicitly mentioned as the proposed model and core solution in tackling the Architect-Builder Problem.
name.quote: Under these constraints, we propose Architect-Builder Iterated Guiding (ABIG), a solution to the Architect-Builder Problem.

is_contributed.justification: ABIG is introduced and developed as a novel solution within the research, presenting a new approach for the problem defined in the paper.
is_contributed.quote: Under these constraints, we propose Architect-Builder Iterated Guiding (ABIG), a solution to the Architect-Builder Problem.

is_executed.justification: The paper presents experiments showing execution and results obtained using the ABIG model, demonstrating its operational capability.
is_executed.quote: We analyze the key learning mechanisms of ABIG and test it in a 2-dimensional instantiation of the ABP.

is_compared.justification: There are comparisons between the ABIG method and other baseline approaches, demonstrating its empirical evaluation against existing models.
is_compared.quote: We apply ABIG to the four learning tasks of BuildWorld and compare it with the two control settings: ABIG-no-intent (no guiding during training) and random (builder takes random actions).

referenced_paper_title.justification: ABIG is an original contribution of this paper and is not attributed to any prior reference paper.

name.justification: BuildWorld is explicitly mentioned as the environment where experiments are conducted, showcasing its use as a dataset for evaluation.
name.quote: We conduct our experiments in BuildWorld. BuildWorld is a 2D construction grid-world of size (w × h).

referenced_paper_title.justification: BuildWorld is described as part of the experimental setup within this paper, not cited from another reference.
referenced_paper_title.quote: We conduct our experiments in BuildWorld.
